title: A finite piece with one point over u survives a further base change with trivial residue field extension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $\varphi:U\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $u\in U$, $s=\varphi(u)$, $x\in X$ with $f(x)=s$. Let $X_U=X\times_SU$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p:X_U\to X$, $q:X_U\to U$, and let $V\subseteq X_U$ be an open subscheme such that (i) $V\hookrightarrow X_U\xrightarrow{q}U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], (ii) there is exactly one point $v\in V$ with $q(v)=u$, (iii) $p(v)=x$ and the map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(v)$ induced by $p$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism. Let $\psi:U'\to U$ be a morphism of schemes and $u'\in U'$ with $\psi(u')=u$ such that $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ (induced by $\psi$) is an isomorphism. Let $X_{U'}=X\times_SU'$ be the fibre product of $f$ and $\varphi\circ\psi$, with projections $p':X_{U'}\to X$, $q':X_{U'}\to U'$, let $\pi:X_{U'}\to X_U$ be the morphism with $p\circ\pi=p'$ and $q\circ\pi=\psi\circ q'$, and let $V'=\pi^{-1}(V)$, an open subscheme of $X_{U'}$. Then (i') $V'\hookrightarrow X_{U'}\xrightarrow{q'}U'$ is finite, (ii') there is exactly one point $v'\in V'$ with $q'(v')=u'$, and (iii') $p'(v')=x$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(v')$ (induced by $p'$) is an isomorphism; moreover $\pi(v')=v$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LK (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-at-point), final assertion (lines 11951-11954: for an elementary etale neighbourhood $(U',u')\to(U,u)$ the triple $(U',u',U'\times_UV)$ again satisfies (i)-(iii)); Stacks gives no proof of it, and its proof of Lemma 02LL (lines 11998-12011) applies it to opens $V_i$ obtained earlier, i.e. to any triple satisfying (i)-(iii). Stated here for an arbitrary $\psi$ with $\kappa(u)\cong\kappa(u')$ (etaleness of $\psi$ is not needed); the agent's formulation.

proof.text: The square $(X_{U'},\pi,q')$ is cartesian over $(q,\psi)$. Consider the commutative diagram with rows $X_{U'}\xrightarrow{\pi}X_U\xrightarrow{p}X$ and $U'\xrightarrow{\psi}U\xrightarrow{\varphi}S$ and columns $q'$, $q$, $f$: it commutes since $q\circ\pi=\psi\circ q'$ and $f\circ p=\varphi\circ q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to it, read with $X'=X_{U'}$, $X=U'$, $Y'=X_U$, $Y=U$, $Z'=X$, $Z=S$ and $a=q'$, $f'=\pi$, $f=\psi$, $b=q$, $h'=p$, $h=\varphi$, $c=f$ (so $fa=bf'$ is $\psi q'=q\pi$ and $hb=ch'$ is $\varphi q=fp$). The lower square is cartesian: $(X_U,q,p)$ is the fibre product of $\varphi$ and $f$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The outer rectangle is cartesian: $(X_{U'},q',p\circ\pi)=(X_{U'},q',p')$ is the fibre product of $\varphi\circ\psi$ and $f$ by definition of $X_{U'}$. Hence the upper square is cartesian: $(X_{U'},\pi,q')$ is a fibre product $X_U\times_UU'$ of $q:X_U\to U$ and $\psi:U'\to U$, with first projection $\pi$ and second projection $q'$.

proof.text: (i') $V'\to U'$ is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to the fibre product $X_{U'}=X_U\times_UU'$ of step 1 (morphisms $q:X_U\to U$, $\psi:U'\to U$, projections $\pi$, $q'$) with the open subschemes $U\subseteq U$, $V\subseteq X_U$, $U'\subseteq U'$ ($q(V)\subseteq U$ and $\psi(U')\subseteq U$ trivially): the canonical morphism $V\times_UU'\to X_{U'}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with image $\pi^{-1}(V)\cap q'^{-1}(U')=\pi^{-1}(V)=V'$, compatibly with the projections. So the open subscheme $V'$, with the morphism $V'\hookrightarrow X_{U'}\xrightarrow{q'}U'$, is isomorphic over $U'$ to $V\times_UU'$ with its second projection, i.e. to the base change of $q|_V:V\to U$ along $\psi$. By hypothesis (i) $q|_V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a) the projection $V\times_UU'\to U'$ is finite, and hence so is $V'\to U'$ (composing with the isomorphism $V'\cong V\times_UU'$ over $U'$, an isomorphism being finite).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LK (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-at-point), final assertion, lines 11951-11954; Stacks gives no proof, the step is the agent's

proof.text: (ii') Exactly one point $v'$ of $V'$ over $u'$, and $\pi(v')=v$. Let $z\in V'$ with $q'(z)=u'$. Then $y=\pi(z)\in V$ and $q(y)=\psi(q'(z))=\psi(u')=u$, so $y=v$ by (ii). Conversely every $z\in X_{U'}$ with $\pi(z)=v$ lies in $\pi^{-1}(V)=V'$. Hence $\{z\in V':q'(z)=u'\}=\pi^{-1}(v)\cap q'^{-1}(u')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], applied to the fibre product $X_{U'}=X_U\times_UU'$ of step 1 (with the points $v\in X_U$, $u'\in U'$, $q(v)=u=\psi(u')$), this set is in bijection with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(v)\otimes_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(u'))$, the maps $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(v)$, $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ being induced by $q$ and $\psi$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Since $r:\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis, $\kappa(v)\to\kappa(v)\otimes_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(u')$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, is a ring isomorphism (inverse $a\otimes b\mapsto a\,r^{-1}(b)$), so the tensor product is a field and its spectrum has exactly one point (the zero ideal). Therefore there is exactly one $v'\in V'$ with $q'(v')=u'$, and $\pi(v')=v$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LK (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-at-point), final assertion, lines 11951-11954; Stacks gives no proof, the step is the agent's

proof.text: (iii') $p'(v')=x$ and $\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(v')$. First $p'(v')=p(\pi(v'))=p(v)=x$ by step 3 and (iii). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] to the fibre product $X_{U'}=X_U\times_UU'$ of step 1 and the point $z=v'$ (so $\pi(z)=v$, $q'(z)=u'$, over $u$): with $R=\kappa(v)\otimes_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(u')$ and $\mathfrak p$ the kernel of $R\to\kappa(v')$, $a\otimes b\mapsto\pi^\sharp(a)q'^\sharp(b)$. By step 3, $R$ is a field, so $\mathfrak p=0$ and $R/\mathfrak p=R$ is a field; hence $R\to\kappa(v')$ is an isomorphism compatible with the maps from $\kappa(v)$, i.e. $\pi^\sharp:\kappa(v)\to\kappa(v')$ is the composite of the isomorphism $\kappa(v)\to R$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, of step 3 and the isomorphism $R\to\kappa(v')$, so $\pi^\sharp$ is an isomorphism. The map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(v')$ induced by $p'=p\circ\pi$ is the composite of $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(v)$ induced by $p$ and $\pi^\sharp$ (the maps on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] come from the maps of local rings $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{X_U,v}\to\mathcal O_{X_{U'},v'}$, whose composite is the map of $p'$); the first is an isomorphism by (iii), so the composite is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks 02LK (more-morphisms.tex 11924-11954; the final assertion is for an elementary etale neighbourhood, and the node's generalization to any psi with kappa(u)=kappa(u') is correct: etaleness is not used). Stacks gives no proof, so the proof is agent-written in four steps: (1) (X_{U'},pi,q') is a fibre product X_U x_U U' by cartesian-square pasting; (2) V'=pi^{-1}(V) is V x_U U' over U' by the open-fibre-product leaf, hence finite over U' by base change of finite morphisms; (3) the points of V' over u' are pi^{-1}(v) cap q'^{-1}(u'), in bijection with Spec(kappa(v) tensor_{kappa(u)} kappa(u')) = Spec kappa(v), one point, by the fibre-product-points leaf; (4) residue field of that point is that tensor product (fibre-product-point-residue-field node), so kappa(v)->kappa(v') and kappa(x)->kappa(v') are isomorphisms. The brief's alternative route through the fibre of a base change (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change) is not needed. No new node: every step uses existing nodes (four Mathlib leaves, one reviewed split node, definitions). stmt_deps kept. The item's own Mathlib searches (three kinds, 2026-10-10) were already recorded; no match.
